demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Being in a natural environment similar to where it happened

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I tell myself the event did not really happen or was not that bad
I force myself to think only positive thoughts
I try to push them out of my mind

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
I always choose where to sit based on how safe or protected I feel

Memory.value: My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together
When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something wrong with me as a person
I have to be on guard all the time
The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: Contamination appraisals are hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another person; for this trauma type, guilt, responsibility, danger, or moral failure would be more coherent than feeling physically dirty/contaminated, absent any assault or bodily violation context.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Other-Blame Rumination: I dwell on what other people have done to me
issues.explanation: Other-blame rumination conflicts with the trauma type and the rest of the profile: the central event is that he accidentally injured another person, while the appraisals emphasize defectiveness and threat rather than victimization by others. Dwelling on what other people have done to me points to a different trauma narrative.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Magical Thinking: I tell myself the event did not really happen or was not that bad
issues.explanation: Magical thinking that the event did not really happen or was not that bad sits awkwardly with the very high-severity profile and with simultaneous endorsement of full sensory reliving plus strong persistent threat and self-defectiveness. Partial minimization can occur, but this item as phrased is in notable tension with the rest of the profile.

vignette: Rajiv's Story Rajiv, an 80-year-old South Asian widower and former Coast Guard member, has been grappling with a traumatic event that occurred decades ago but continues to haunt him. The event took place during his service in the Coast Guard when he accidentally caused serious injury to another crewmember. Since then, Rajiv has found himself caught in a cycle of distressing memories and avoidance behaviors. On a fateful day, Rajiv was operating machinery on their vessel when an unforeseen malfunction led to an accident. He vividly remembers the sound of the machinery and the sudden jolt that sent his colleague sprawling onto the deck. The sight of blood and hearing the frantic cries for help are etched in his memory as fragmented pieces that do not form a coherent narrative. Since then, Rajiv has developed numerous triggers that activate intense distress. Being in natural environments similar to where the incident occurred-like the coastline or any open water-brings back vivid, full sensory reliving of the event. The sound of sirens is particularly jarring, as it evokes memories of emergency response efforts after the accident. Rajiv's coping mechanisms have been both his refuge and his prison. He often tells himself that the event did not really happen or was not that bad, engaging in magical thinking to soothe his mind. Additionally, he forces himself to think only positive thoughts, a form of positive reframing that helps him momentarily escape the grip of his distress. However, these strategies have also led Rajiv down a path of avoidance and hypervigilance. He avoids going to unfamiliar places because he cannot assess the danger, always seeking safety and protection in familiar environments. Even within the comfort of his home, he carefully chooses where to sit based on how safe or protected he feels. The fragmented nature of his memories has made it difficult for Rajiv to recall the event deliberately. When a memory does come back, it is often sudden and overwhelming, making him feel as though he is reliving every detail across all senses at once. This has led him to engage in thought suppression, trying to push these memories out of his mind. Rajiv's negative appraisals are deeply rooted in feelings of defectiveness and blame. He firmly believes that there is something fundamentally wrong with him as a person and that the event happened because he was the type of person it did. This belief has made it challenging for him to trust himself and others, leading to risky behavior at times as if to prove his worth or distract from his distress. Over time, these behaviors have taken a toll on Rajiv's daily life and relationships. He avoids going out into nature or places that remind him of the accident, which has limited his social interactions and activities. His hypervigilance makes it difficult for him to relax in any environment, leading to strained interactions with family and friends. What finally brought Rajiv to seek help was a recent incident where he experienced an intense flashback while driving near the coast. The sudden onset of distress and fear left him shaken and unable to continue his daily routines. He realized that he could no longer avoid or suppress his memories indefinitely, nor could he bear the isolation they imposed. Rajiv is most afraid of never finding peace with what happened, haunted by a sense of guilt and inadequacy. However, he also hopes for a chance to regain some semblance of control over his life, to be able to engage in activities without constant fear, and to reconnect with others in meaningful ways. His journey toward healing is just beginning, but he knows that confronting these memories and understanding them within the context of his traumatic experience may help him find a path forward.
